scope: 24 major public commercial airports in Nigeria (7 federally designated scheduled international passenger gateways and 17 major domestic commercial airports, including seasonal Hajj and cargo-capable terminals), manually verified from FAAN, NCAA, Federal Ministry of Aviation, state airport portals, and established aeronautical references. Excludes military airbases, private oil-company helipads, and unscheduled bush airstrips.
notes: Classification reflects regular scheduled passenger designation as verified on 2026-10-23: 'international' covers the 7 gateways designated by the Federal Government for scheduled cross-border passenger traffic (Lagos, Abuja, Kano, Port Harcourt, Enugu, Uyo, and Maiduguri). Several Nigerian domestic commercial airports carry 'International' in their ceremonial or cargo names or handle seasonal Hajj charters while operating scheduled domestic passenger routes; those nuances are stated explicitly per airport. Unassigned global IATA codes are omitted rather than guessed. NaijaCheck does not display live flight status, ticket fares, or booking schedules.

airports.name: Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport
airports.runwayNote: Single 3,610 m × 60 m asphalt runway (04/22); separate international terminal (commissioned December 2018) and General Aviation / domestic wing.
airports.operationsNote: Primary diplomatic and capital-city gateway serving Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory with scheduled international flights across Africa, Europe, and the Middle East alongside Nigeria's second-busiest domestic trunk network. Recertified by the NCAA under Nig.CARs Part 12 in November 2024.

airports.notes: Located roughly 20–40 km southwest of central Abuja districts (Garki, Wuse, Maitama) along the Umaru Musa Yar'Adua Expressway.

airports.name: Akure Airport
airports.runwayNote: 2,800 m × 45 m asphalt runway (03R/21L) published in FAAN domestic aerodrome specifications.
airports.operationsNote: Commissioned on 8 February 1986 as a domestic commercial airport serving Akure and Ondo State, about 12 km east of Akure city centre at Obale. Named Olumuyiwa Bernard Aliu Airport in the June 2023 federal aviation directive in honour of the Nigerian former President of the ICAO Council.

airports.notes: Serves scheduled domestic flights linking Ondo and neighbouring Ekiti communities to Lagos and Abuja.

airports.name: Chinua Achebe International Cargo and Passenger Airport
airports.operator: Anambra State Government (Anambra Airport City Infrastructure Limited), with FAAN safety/firefighting partnership
airports.runwayNote: 3,700 m asphalt runway (06/24) designed for wide-body cargo and commercial passenger aircraft.
airports.operationsNote: Inaugurated on 30 October 2021 by the Anambra State Government, cleared by the NCAA for commercial passenger flights in December 2021, and renamed after literary icon Chinua Achebe on 1 October 2023. Operates scheduled domestic commercial routes linking the Onitsha–Awka–Nnewi commercial corridor to Lagos and Abuja.

OurAirports — Nigeria Anambra State Aerodrome Record (DNAN)

airports.notes: Official ICAO location indicator is DNAN. Global 3-letter IATA code is omitted here because international aeronautical registries record no assigned IATA code for Umueri (in IATA's global directory, ANA is assigned to Anaa Airport, French Polynesia, although Nigerian domestic airline booking engines use ANA as a local booking code).

airports.name: Asaba International Airport
airports.operator: Asaba Airport Company Limited (30-year PPP concession from Delta State Government signed February 2021)
airports.runwayNote: 3,400 m asphalt runway (11/29) rehabilitated and upgraded to NCAA Category 6 standards.
airports.operationsNote: State-owned commercial airport serving Delta State's capital Asaba as well as the neighbouring Onitsha commercial bridgehead across the River Niger. Operated under a 30-year public-private concession by Asaba Airport Company Limited with scheduled domestic passenger flights to Lagos and Abuja.

airports.name: Benin Airport
airports.runwayNote: 2,400 m × 45 m asphalt runway (05R/23L) published by FAAN.
airports.operationsNote: Constructed in 1956 during the colonial aviation expansion and located roughly 2 km southwest of central Benin City in Edo State. One of Nigeria's busiest South-South domestic commercial airports, renamed Oba Akenzua II Airport under the June 2023 federal naming directive.

sources.label: FAAN — Domestic Airports: Benin Airport Profile (official)

airports.notes: Handles high-frequency scheduled domestic passenger flights to Lagos and Abuja.

airports.name: Margaret Ekpo International Airport
airports.runwayNote: 2,450 m × 45 m asphalt runway (03R/21L) listed on FAAN's domestic airports directory.
airports.operationsNote: Commissioned in 1983 and named after pioneering Nigerian women's rights activist Margaret Ekpo. Grouped within FAAN's Domestic Airports network, serving scheduled domestic commercial traffic for Calabar, Tinapa, and Cross River State alongside occasional regional charter flights.

airports.runwayNote: 3,000 m asphalt runway (08/26) at Emene; emergency runway rehabilitation completed with flight resumption on 28 April 2025.
airports.operationsNote: Designated South-East international gateway listed among FAAN's 5 core international airports, named after elder statesman Dr. Akanu Ibiam. Serves scheduled international connections (such as Addis Ababa) and major domestic routes across southeastern Nigeria.

airports.name: Brigadier Zakari Maimalari Airport
airports.operator: Gombe State Government (Sole Administrator management pending completion of Federal Government / FAAN handover; NAMA air traffic services)
airports.runwayNote: 3,000 m asphalt runway capable of handling narrow-body commercial jets and seasonal Hajj wide-body charters.
airports.operationsNote: Located near Lawanti village in Akko LGA along the Bauchi–Gombe highway. Renamed Brigadier Zakari Maimalari Airport in June 2023. Serves scheduled domestic passenger flights to Abuja alongside seasonal Hajj pilgrim airlifts certified by the NCAA.

airports.name: Ibadan Airport
airports.runwayNote: 2,400 m × 45 m asphalt runway (05R/23L) published by FAAN, with Oyo State-backed runway and terminal expansion works initiated for larger jet capability.
airports.operationsNote: Commissioned in June 1982 at Alakia between Adegbaiji community and Iwo Road on the eastern edge of Ibadan. Renamed Samuel Ladoke Akintola Airport in the June 2023 federal aviation directive; serves domestic commercial traffic across Oyo and Osun states.

airports.name: General Tunde Idiagbon International Airport
airports.runwayNote: 3,100 m × 60 m asphalt runway (05R/23L) published by FAAN — designated primary diversion alternate for Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos.
airports.operationsNote: Commissioned on 16 February 1978 and renamed General Tunde Idiagbon International Airport in June 2023. Listed under FAAN's Domestic Airports directory for regular scheduled passenger routes (Abuja and Lagos), while also serving seasonal Hajj charters and wide-body weather diversions from Lagos.

airports.name: Yakubu Gowon Airport
airports.runwayNote: 3,000 m × 45 m asphalt runway (10/28) at roughly 1,290 m (4,232 ft) elevation — Nigeria's highest-altitude commercial airport.
airports.operationsNote: Located at Heipang in Barkin Ladi LGA, approximately 30 km south of Jos city centre, and named after former Head of State General Yakubu Gowon. Operates scheduled domestic flights and agro-cargo initiatives under a FAAN–Plateau State infrastructure partnership.

airports.name: Kaduna Airport
airports.runwayNote: 3,000 m × 60 m asphalt runway (05R/23L) published by FAAN, located roughly 12 km northwest of Kaduna metropolis.
airports.operationsNote: Commissioned in 1982 under the Nigerian Airports Authority (now FAAN) as the civil commercial aerodrome distinct from the older military airfield inside Kaduna city. Renamed after former Northern Region military governor Major General Hassan Usman Katsina in June 2023; operates scheduled domestic routes and seasonal Hajj charters.

airports.name: Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport
airports.runwayNote: Primary 3,301 m × 60 m asphalt runway (06/24) plus secondary 2,451 m runway (05/23); separate domestic and international terminals.
airports.operationsNote: Nigeria's oldest airport — air operations began in 1936 — and the primary international aviation hub for Northern Nigeria. Handles year-round scheduled international passenger flights (Middle East, North and East Africa), major Hajj airlifts, and domestic trunk routes; certified by the NCAA.

airports.name: Umaru Musa Yar'Adua Airport
airports.runwayNote: 3,045 m × 45 m asphalt runway (05R/23L) published on FAAN's domestic airports directory.
airports.operationsNote: Commenced operations on 22 December 1991 about 4 km southwest of Katsina metropolis and named in honour of former President Umaru Musa Yar'Adua. Operates scheduled domestic flights to Abuja and seasonal Hajj pilgrim charters.

airports.name: Murtala Muhammed International Airport
airports.operator: Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN); Domestic Terminal 2 (MMA2) operated under PPP concession by Bi-Courtney Aviation Services Limited (BASL)
airports.runwayNote: Dual parallel asphalt runways — 18R/36L (3,900 m × 60 m) for wide-body international traffic and 18L/36R (2,743 m × 45 m) near the domestic terminals.
airports.operationsNote: Nigeria's busiest international and domestic aviation hub, situated in Ikeja, Lagos State. Comprises International Terminals 1 and 2 (T2 commissioned March 2022) on the international side, plus the FAAN General Aviation Terminal (GAT / MMA1) and private PPP terminal MMA2 on the domestic side; recertified by the NCAA in November 2024.

airports.name: General Muhammadu Buhari International Airport
airports.runwayNote: 3,000 m × 60 m asphalt runway (05R/23L) published by FAAN.
airports.operationsNote: Established as an airstrip in the 1950s, expanded in the 1980s, renamed General Muhammadu Buhari Airport in June 2023, and upgraded by Presidential and Federal Ministry of Aviation approval (October 2024 / March 2025) as the designated international gateway for Nigeria's North-East geopolitical zone.

airports.runwayNote: 2,996 m × 50 m runway (05R/23L) with 266 m paved overrun on each end, published verbatim by FAAN (IATA: MDI, ICAO: DNMK).
airports.operationsNote: Civil enclave commenced commercial operations in 1983 at Fili along the Makurdi–Gboko highway in Benue State. Renamed Joseph Sarwuan Tarka Airport in June 2023; handles domestic commercial flights to Abuja and charter movements.

airports.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Airport
airports.operator: Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), with terminal/agro-cargo upgrade partnership by Niger State Government
airports.runwayNote: 3,400 m × 44 m asphalt runway (05R/23L) published verbatim by FAAN (IATA: MXJ, ICAO: DNMN).
airports.operationsNote: Commissioned on 20 June 1990 in Maikunkele, Bosso LGA, 10 km northwest of Minna. Renamed Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Airport in March 2024 following Niger State terminal and agro-cargo upgrades, with scheduled domestic commercial passenger flights resuming in April 2025 alongside seasonal Hajj operations.

airports.name: Sam Mbakwe International Cargo Airport
airports.runwayNote: 2,700 m × 45 m asphalt runway (17/35) at 114 m (374 ft) elevation.
airports.operationsNote: Nigeria's first community-funded state-initiated airport, conceived under Governor Sam Mbakwe, commissioned in 1994, and managed by FAAN. Situated in Ngor Okpala LGA (~23 km southeast of Owerri), it is one of southeastern Nigeria's busiest domestic passenger hubs, serving Imo State as well as Aba and Umuahia in neighbouring Abia State.

airports.name: Port Harcourt International Airport
airports.runwayNote: 3,000 m × 60 m asphalt runway (03/21); dedicated international terminal (commissioned October 2018) and domestic terminal.
airports.operationsNote: Primary international gateway for the Niger Delta oil, gas, and maritime hub at Omagwa in Ikwerre LGA, Rivers State — one of FAAN's 5 core international airports and certified by the NCAA. Handles scheduled international flights to Europe and regional hubs plus dense domestic services to Lagos and Abuja.

airports.name: Sultan Abubakar III International Airport
airports.runwayNote: 3,000 m × 60 m asphalt runway (08R/26L) published by FAAN.
airports.operationsNote: Commissioned on 17 February 1982 and named after the 17th Sultan of Sokoto, Sir Siddiq Abubakar III. Listed on FAAN's Domestic Airports directory for year-round scheduled domestic flights (Abuja and Kano/Lagos connections) while serving as a major North-West Hajj and Umrah international charter hub.

airports.name: Victor Attah International Airport
airports.operator: Akwa Ibom State Government (Ibom Airport Development Company Limited), with FAAN/NCAA/NAMA regulatory and security services
airports.runwayNote: 3,600 m Category II runway with Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) hangar complex and international passenger terminal.
airports.operationsNote: Opened in 2009, renamed after former Governor Obong Victor Attah in November 2018, and home base of state-owned carrier Ibom Air. Officially designated for full international flight operations by the Federal Government on 27 November 2025, inaugurating scheduled cross-border Uyo–Accra commercial service on 2 May 2026.

airports.name: Osubi Airport
airports.operator: Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) — managing operations since March 2021 on behalf of the NNPCL joint-venture owners
airports.runwayNote: 1,800 m usable landing runway (45 m wide), suited to regional turboprop and light jet commercial aircraft.
airports.operationsNote: Commissioned in April 1999 in Osubi town (Okpe LGA), about 10 km northeast of Effurun and Warri in Delta State, and reopened under FAAN management in 2021. Renamed Alfred Diete-Spiff Airport in June 2023; operates scheduled domestic passenger routes to Lagos and Abuja.

Listed under FAAN's Domestic Airports directory for regular scheduled domestic flights to Abuja and Lagos, plus seasonal Hajj pilgrim operations.
